items.stem: In a transformer, what does the self-attention mechanism primarily allow each token to do?

options.text: Weight and combine information from other tokens in the sequence
options.rationale: Correct: attention lets each token attend to relevant others.

options.text: Remove the need for any training data

options.rationale: Attention does not ensure factual correctness.

items.stem: Which TWO are appropriate reasons to use retrieval-augmented generation instead of a very long prompt? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The knowledge base is large and changes over time
options.rationale: Correct: retrieval scales and stays current without re-stuffing prompts.

options.text: You want to cite the source passages used
You want the model to hallucinate more freely
options.rationale: RAG aims to reduce, not increase, hallucination.

options.text: You want to avoid storing any documents

items.explanation: Correct: retrieval scales and stays current without re-stuffing prompts.

items.stem: Why can a fluent, confident model answer still be wrong?

options.text: Generative models optimise plausible continuations, not verified facts
options.rationale: Correct: fluency reflects likelihood, not truth.

options.text: The model cannot produce grammatical text
options.rationale: It can; the issue is factual grounding.

options.text: Confidence scores are a guaranteed accuracy measure
